the study of the electrochemical reduction of organic compounds and the electrocarboxylic reaction.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrochemical carboxylation of aromatic ketones in dimethylformamde proceeds via a mixed ECE- DISP mechanism, the ECE step being the rate determining step.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the electrochemical carboxylation reaction of aromatic ketones in dimethylformamde is a two-step reaction, the first step being the attack of the electrogenerated RR'CO_ − at CO 2 and the second one being the reduction of the adduct formed in the first step followed by a second attack at CO 2.
the mechanism of the electrocar boxylation of ketones is the same in DMF and in MeCN, the solvent being able to exert only a quantitative effect on the rate constant of the reaction.

the electrocarboxylations of the aromatic ketones in DMF proceed via an initial ECE step, followed by a DISP1 step, which leads to the formation of the corresponding carboxylic acids in a single step.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electrocarboxylative process is not limited to aromatic ketones bearing electron-withdrawing substituents.

the electrochemical carboalkoxylation reaction of aromatic ketones in dimethylformdiamide is a two-step reaction, involving a first carboxylation of the electrogenerated radical anion and a second one of a further electrogenerated radical anions.
the carboxylation reaction proceeds through an ECE-DISC1 mechanism and that the first reduction step of the reaction (E) is always rate-determining.
